cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. Back in Leviticus 13, it was all about how a priest spots a skin disease. Now God gives the law for the best day of all: the day the person gets cleansed.

cards.question: On the day of cleansing, where does the priest go to examine the person with the skin disease?

cards.text: He's out there to check one thing: has the skin disease healed? A HOUSE CALL, friend! I sat in a junk drawer for years and never got one of those.

cards.question: If the skin disease has healed, the priest orders two live clean ___ to be brought, plus cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.

cards.text: The priest commands that one of the birds be slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot. Fresh water, clay pot. Very specific, just the way I like my recipes.

cards.question: The priest has the second bird slaughtered too.

cards.text: That second bird stays alive. The priest takes it, along with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop, and dips them all into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered.

cards.question: Next the priest sprinkles the one being cleansed of the skin disease. How many times?
After the sprinkling, the priest pronounces the person clean.
The priest still has the live bird that was dipped in the blood. What happens to it?

answers.text: It's released into the open field
It's offered up on the altar
It's given to the priest's family

cards.text: Next, the person washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair and bathes with water, and he's ceremonially clean. He can come back into the camp, but there's a catch.

cards.question: The person being cleansed is back in the camp. For seven days, where must he stay?

cards.text: That's standing on the porch for a WEEK with your keys sitting on the kitchen counter. Then on the seventh day, it's time to shave all over again.

cards.question: On the seventh day, the person shaves off his hair again, but he gets to keep his eyebrows.

cards.text: Head, beard, EYEBROWS, all of it, and with these eyebrows I'd need a second week. Then he washes his clothes and bathes, and he will be clean.

On the eighth day, he brings two unblemished male lambs, an unblemished ewe lamb a year old, fine flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, and a log of olive oil. That's a lot to carry, friend.

cards.question: The priest presents the person and all these offerings before the LORD. Where?

answers.text: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
Out in the open field by the camp
Beside the river outside the camp

cards.text: The priest takes one male lamb as a guilt offering and waves it with the log of olive oil before the LORD. Then he slaughters it in the sanctuary area, where the sin offering and burnt offering are slaughtered.

cards.question: Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest.

cards.text: Now the priest takes some of the blood from the guilt offering and puts it on the one being cleansed, in three spots.

cards.question: Where does the priest put the blood of the guilt offering on the one being cleansed?

answers.text: His right earlobe and thumb and big toe
His forehead and both of his palms
His chest and both of his shoulders

cards.text: Then the oil: the priest pours some into his left palm, dips his right forefinger in it and sprinkles it seven times before the LORD. Me? I measure chocolate chips by squinting and going, eh, that looks right.

cards.question: The priest puts some of the oil on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe of the one being cleansed, right on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
There's still oil left in the priest's palm. He puts the rest of it on the ___ of the one being cleansed.

cards.text: The priest puts it there to make atonement for him before the LORD. Then the priest sacrifices the sin offering, and then the burnt offering along with the grain offering.

cards.question: With all the offerings made, the priest makes atonement for him, and he will be ___.

cards.text: But what if the person is poor and can't afford all those offerings? Friend, I was bought for a quarter at a bakery's closing sale, so I LIKE where this is going.

cards.question: A poor person can skip the lamb and bring only birds for his cleansing.
Along with the lamb, the poor person brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons. How does he choose which?

cards.text: On the eighth day the priest walks through the same steps: the wave offering, the blood and oil on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe, and the rest of the oil on his head. Then come the two birds, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and the priest makes atonement for him before the LORD.
Then the LORD speaks to Moses and Aaron the priest, and now it's about houses. It's for when they enter the land He's giving them, and He puts mildew into a house there.

cards.question: God is looking ahead to the land He's giving Israel as their possession: the land of ___.

cards.text: The owner comes and tells the priest, "Something like mildew has appeared in my house." Something LIKE mildew, friend, and I bet that man knows EXACTLY what it is.

cards.question: Before the priest goes in to examine the mildew, what has to happen to the house?

answers.text: It has to be cleared out
It has to be swept clean
It has to be lit with lamps

cards.text: The reason? So nothing in the house becomes unclean. Smart. Get the couch out BEFORE the verdict.
Inside, the priest looks for green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall. If that's what he finds, he steps outside the doorway and closes the house up.

cards.question: After finding the mildew, the priest closes up the house for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest comes back, and the mildew has spread on the walls. What happens to the contaminated stones?

answers.text: Pulled out and thrown outside the city
Washed off and put back in place
Carried in and burned on the altar

cards.text: The inside gets scraped completely, and the plaster goes to an unclean place outside the city. New stones and fresh mortar go in, and that's not cleaning, friend, that's a RENOVATION.

cards.question: If the mildew comes back and spreads after the new stones and plaster, what happens to the house?

answers.text: It's torn down and hauled outside the city
It's closed up for another seven days
It's scraped and replastered all over again

cards.text: Stones, timbers, plaster, all of it, out to an unclean place outside the city. I spent years in a junk drawer full of paper and dust, and if a priest had inspected it, I'd have been hauled out with the timbers.

cards.question: Anyone who walks into the house while it's closed up stays unclean for seven days.
Anyone who sleeps or eats in a house closed up because of mildew must wash his ___.

cards.text: But if the priest inspects after the replastering and the mildew hasn't spread, he pronounces the house clean, because the mildew is gone. Best inspection report EVER.

cards.question: To purify the clean house, the priest takes two ___ along with cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.

cards.text: Same recipe as the person's cleansing: one bird is slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot. The priest dips the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet yarn and live bird in the blood and the fresh water, and sprinkles the house seven times.

cards.question: In the house's cleansing, the live bird is offered on the altar.

cards.text: In this way he makes atonement for the house, and it will be clean. Then God wraps it all up: this is the law for skin diseases, scaly outbreaks, mildew in clothing or a house, and any swelling, rash or spot.

cards.question: God wraps up the whole law about skin diseases and mildew. What is it all for?

answers.text: To tell when something is clean or unclean
To decide who can serve as a priest
To set the days for the yearly feasts

cards.text: And that's where we'll set it down for now, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this teaching on clean and unclean isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The card says Leviticus 13 'was all about how a priest spots a skin disease.' Leviticus 13 also covers mildew in clothing (Lev 13:47-59), so 'all about' skin disease misstates the earlier chapter.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards can only be answered by luck. No story card sets up the answers to card 2 (outside the camp), card 4 (birds), card 8 (seven times), card 10 (bird released into the field) or card 12 (outside his tent). That is 5 discovery questions out of 8 choice cards. Add context on the story cards or ask questions the baker can reason out.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Card 11 asks about the line 'and he will be clean' (Lev 14:20). The baker already heard that line at Lev 14:9 (stop 1, card 15), so this asks about a repeated line again.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'It has to be swept clean' is close in meaning to the right answer 'It has to be cleared out.' A baker could argue that clearing a house means cleaning it out.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 15 asks about the 'two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop' line (Lev 14:49). That line repeats Lev 14:4, which stop 1, card 4 already asked about with the same answers (birds, rams, goats).

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Card 17 asks what happens to the live bird. Its release into the open field (Lev 14:53) repeats Lev 14:7, which stop 1, card 10 already asked about. Card 17 even reuses that card's wrong answer about the altar. Card 16 also tells the baker it's the 'same recipe,' which gives the answer away.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: In stop 1, card 5, Papa Dorin says a very specific recipe is 'just the way I like my recipes.' Here he says he measures chocolate chips 'by squinting.' His two made-up baking habits contradict each other within the same lesson.
findings.question: Must the small habits Papa Dorin makes up in jokes stay consistent with each other within one lesson?

findings.problem: The last card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage, but it cites Leviticus 14:57. Card 19 already covers that verse.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should it cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
